page_01: A wet dog can shake most of the water out of its fur in about four seconds!
page_02: Kittens practice pouncing when they play. It's how they learn to hunt.
page_03: A happy bunny jumps and twists in the air. It's called a binky!
page_04: Hamsters carry food in stretchy cheek pouches that reach back to their shoulders!
page_05: Pet goldfish can learn to recognize the person who feeds them.
page_06: Retriever dogs got their name because they love to fetch things and bring them back.
page_07: A cat's whiskers help it feel its way around and tell if it fits through a gap.
page_08: Happy guinea pigs hop straight up in the air. It's called popcorning!
page_09: Some pet parrots can learn to say more than 100 words!
page_10: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton, so it can never take it off.
page_11: A pony is a small horse. Ponies stand less than about 58 inches tall at the shoulder.
page_12: Dachshunds were bred to dig into burrows. Their name means badger dog!
page_13: Corgis were bred to herd cows. Their short legs keep them low to the ground.
page_14: Long ago, pugs were the favorite pets of emperors in China.
page_15: Dalmatian puppies are born with no spots. Their spots appear as they grow!
page_16: A beagle's nose has over 200 million scent sensors. Yours has about 5 million!
page_17: Poodles were first bred to swim out and fetch ducks from the water.
page_18: The chihuahua is the smallest dog breed in the world.
page_19: Cats sleep about 12 to 16 hours a day. That's a lot of naps!
page_20: Cats purr when they're happy, and sometimes to calm themselves down.
page_21: Cats can twist in the air to land on their feet. It's called the righting reflex!
page_22: A kitten's tongue is covered in tiny hooks that work like a comb.
page_23: Cats can jump up to about five times their own height!
page_24: Cats press soft blankets with their paws. People call it making biscuits!
page_25: A rabbit can turn each of its long ears a different way to listen.
page_26: Rabbits mostly eat hay. Carrots are just a small treat!
page_27: A pet hamster can run for miles on its wheel in a single night!
page_28: Guinea pigs often squeak 'wheek wheek' when they hear the fridge open!
page_29: Budgies are small parrots that come from Australia.
page_30: Some tortoises live to be more than 100 years old!
page_31: A hedgehog has about 5,000 to 7,000 spines to keep it safe!
page_32: Crested geckos can't blink, so they lick their eyes to keep them clean!
page_33: An axolotl can grow back a lost leg, and even parts of its heart!
page_34: Happy ferrets hop around and make a chuckling sound called dooking.
page_35: Chinchillas take dust baths instead of water baths to keep their thick fur clean.
page_36: Ponies and horses can sleep standing up without falling over!
page_37: Puppies and kittens that grow up together often become best friends.
page_38: Most pets visit the vet for a check-up at least once a year, just like you!
page_39: Dogs tend to wag their tails more to the right when they're happy to see you.
page_40: Puppies have 28 baby teeth. Grown-up dogs have 42!
page_41: Many families celebrate the day their pet came home. It's called a gotcha day!
page_42: Kittens are born with their eyes closed. They open after about one to two weeks.
page_43: Dogs bury bones to save them for later, like a hidden snack!
page_44: Cats can see in light about six times dimmer than people need.
page_45: A rabbit's front teeth never stop growing, so rabbits chew a lot!
page_46: Labrador dogs have webbed toes that help them swim!
page_47: Male betta fish blow bubble nests at the top of the water.
page_48: Cockatiels raise the crest on their heads when they're excited or curious.
page_49: Puppies dream like people do. Twitchy paws may mean a dream about running!
page_50: Thanks for coloring with the Pawsome Cuties. Give your pet a big hug!
